issues.failure_explanation: The linear wave problems for v_j and v_0 impose zero data at t=0 (resp. t=T) while also prescribing arbitrary boundary data f_j (resp. f_0) on the lateral boundary. Without compatibility f_j(·,0)=0 and f_0(·,T)=0, the stated solutions in the claimed Sobolev regularity need not exist, so the higher-order linearization and integral identity are not justified for the full stated class of boundary data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard compatibility conditions f_j(·,0)=0 for all j and f_0(·,T)=0, or restrict the DN-map data to zero initial/final trace spaces.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order linearization construction and the reconstruction formulas derived from it are only valid for compatible boundary data, whereas the source states them for general H^{s+1} boundary data.
issues.title: Missing initial/final compatibility for boundary data
issues.why_classification: A local standard compatibility condition repairs the premise; all substantive reconstruction claims survive for compatible data.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the Radon reconstruction invokes a lemma that requires the function to be Lipschitz and compactly supported on all of R^{n+1}. The potential q is only assumed to be C^s on Ω×[0,T]. A zero extension of q to R^{n+1} need not be Lipschitz, and no compactly supported Lipschitz extension is assumed or constructed. Thus the lemma is applied outside its hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use the noise level $\sigma=2\,\%$ in all our examples.

issues.failure_explanation: If the added noise has standard deviation 0.02 times the mean magnitude of the measurement, the power SNR is 10 log10(1/0.02^2)≈34 dB, equivalently 20 log10(1/0.02)≈34 dB. A 44 dB SNR would correspond to a relative standard deviation of about 0.6%, not 2%. The stated numerical claim is therefore incorrect.

issues.overall_effect: The noise level of the numerical experiments is misrepresented, which can mislead comparison of the reconstruction methods.
issues.title: Incorrect SNR calculation for 2% noise
